featured_reviews.name: Spandan Maskar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely disappointing experience and borderline misleading pricing.

I called the salon beforehand and clearly asked for the price of a men’s haircut. I was told it would be Rs 400. Based on that, I went ahead and got my haircut done. Once everything was finished, I was suddenly told my total bill was Rs 630 because I had received a “stylish” haircut.

Naturally, I asked what exactly counts as a normal haircut. The barber’s answer was vague and unhelpful. He just kept repeating “sir, normal haircut,” without explaining anything. When I pushed further, he said my mullet haircut is considered stylish, while a “normal” haircut is just normal. That explanation makes no sense. My hairstyle is not unusual, and I’ve been to many salons before. This is the first time I’ve been charged extra after the service without being informed upfront.

It gets worse. During the haircut, I asked how much a beard trim would cost. The barber casually said Rs 450. I questioned this immediately because I had just been told the haircut itself was Rs 400. How does a beard cost more than the haircut? His response was that Lakme provides them with a rate card and they have to follow it. featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Sathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Florian Juhu – Honest & Constructive Feedback
What brings me to Florian Juhu today is not the brand or the interiors, but the people.

The team that has transitioned from Geetanjali Salon Juhu—Megha, Caroline, Shivam, Ibrahim, Annie, Priya, Neelima, Hritik, Krish, and Hanumesh—is outstanding. I have taken services from them for over three years, and their excellence lies not just in skill, but in consistency, warmth, and genuine personal attention for every client.

Today’s services:
Nails by Annie
Root touch-up, hair wash and blow-dry by Caroline
Foot massage by Hritik
All were excellent.

Additionally Shivam, Krishna, Neelima, Priya and Ibrahim together with others will only do wonders to the brand provided you look into key suggestions mentioned below too.

When Akash (Business Development Manager) asked how the services were and I said excellent, he responded, “That’s us.” It was important for me to clarify that what I meant—and what he also knew I meant—was that the excellence comes from this very team that has moved from Geetanjali. They are what makes the services exceptional. Geetanjali’s loss is clearly Florian’s gain. Preserve them!
Megha, in particular, is extremely capable and will prove her worth even more over time.

The salon itself has a pleasant vibe and is well done up. The grey uniforms look elegant and youthful.

Key Suggestions:

Pricing needs urgent rethinking.
For core, repeat services like wash and blow-dry, ₹1,500–₹2,000 + GST is steep, especially for regular clients. Even legacy luxury salons like Taj have remained more realistic.
I run an organisation of 135 employees, and post-COVID dynamics have compelled us to bring pricing below what we would traditionally consider “fair”, while still maintaining the highest quality standards. This shift is no longer theoretical—it is operational reality.

Pricing cannot rest on “this is Florian and this is how it is.”
People dont care for the kimono or variety of beverages or pick up, pick up drop services, or the peacock look after the hairwash with the towel strip by the hairline.

Keep things simple and practical.
- I refused the kimono—it felt unnecessary and adds to avoidable costs.
- After the hair wash, the narrow towel strip along the hairline, folded into a little flower on top, neither held my wet hair nor looked graceful—it honestly made me look like a peacock. I showed this to the counter staff and told her how ridiculous it looked. A proper full towel wrap is essential.

Staff comfort matters.
Employees should not feel watched constantly. When staff feel heard and trusted, half the job is already done—much like a doctor who reassures a patient before treatment.

Understand your real clientele.
Many clients will be over 45, coming regularly for root touch-ups, wash & blow-dry, or nails. These are repeat services—pricing must reflect frequency, not novelty.

Interiors need a rethink in parts.
The broken-wall effect behind styling counters looks tacky and unfinished.

Valet service needs improvement.
Confusion around parking and poor communication create a poor first impression.

Pick-up and drop service
Review actual usage. If it does not work, discontinue—it will reduce costs.

I have raised similar pricing concerns earlier at Florian Waterfield Road as well—both visits were driven by necessity, not choice.

Final thought:
Florian Hurel and the investors must remain grounded. A brand is ultimately known for its people. Training and SOPs matter, but the art is in the hands of the staff—and clients return because of them. Pricing that ignores ground reality will eventually undo even the best talent.

Shared sincerely, in the hope this feedback is received in the spirit of improvement.
